name: WY at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Democrat Lisa Kinney raised only ~$18k with no outside support
Republican Chuck Gray heavily funded with ~$1.6M outside backing
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~98%
model.rationale: Wyoming's R+23 lean makes this seat effectively unwinnable for Democrats in a general election, and the resource gap is extreme: Gray has raised $1.6 million with substantial outside support while Kinney has raised under $20,000. Markets price a Republican win near certainty, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Gray or a late surge of Democratic outside spending would be the only plausible path to shifting this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Harriet Hageman (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Wyoming's at-large House seat is among the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+23. Harriet Hageman's retirement to run for Senate leaves an open seat, but the Republican nominee, Chuck Gray, starts with overwhelming advantages. He has raised $1.6 million and benefits from roughly $1.6 million in outside support, while outside groups have also spent over $700,000 opposing him in what was a contested primary.

The Democratic nominee, Lisa Kinney, has raised under $20,000 and has no outside backing, leaving her with minimal resources to compete statewide. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 98 percent. With no polls and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Republican hold of roughly twenty points.
